stem: A 68-year-old with COPD sits leaning forward with hands on knees, breathing through pursed lips. Which finding most specifically indicates increased work of breathing?
options: Use of accessory muscles of inspiration
rationale: Accessory muscle recruitment signals that the patient is generating additional negative intrathoracic pressure to meet ventilatory demand and is a classic sign of increased WOB.

stem: During vocal fremitus assessment the vibrations are decreased over the right lower lung field. Which is the most likely cause?
rationale: Fluid in the pleural space (effusion) dampens transmission of sound, reducing fremitus. Consolidation increases fremitus.

stem: A patient with severe asthma has marked intercostal retractions on inspiration. What does this most directly suggest?
rationale: Retractions reflect the patient generating very negative intrathoracic pressure to overcome high airway resistance in obstructive states like asthma.
source_refs: Built from standard critical-care respiratory concepts (assessment, ABG/acid–base, oxygen therapy/devices, imaging & diagnostics, ventilation mechanics).

stem: Which combination best supports cor pulmonale in a patient with chronic bronchitis?
options: Central cyanosis, hypotension, narrow pulse pressure
Pleural friction rub, sharp lateral chest pain
rationale: Chronic hypoxemia → pulmonary HTN → RVH/RVF (cor pulmonale): JVD, hepatomegaly, peripheral edema; cyanosis may be present.

stem: In a dark‑skinned patient, which site is best to detect central cyanosis from hypoxemia?
rationale: Central (warm) cyanosis is best seen on the lips and oral mucosa regardless of skin pigmentation.

stem: Which breathing pattern is most consistent with metabolic acidosis from DKA?
rationale: DKA produces metabolic acidosis; the compensatory pattern is deep, rapid Kussmaul respirations.

stem: You auscultate bronchial breath sounds over the right lower posterior lung field. What does this imply?
rationale: Bronchial quality outside the trachea/main bronchi indicates consolidation that transmits high‑frequency sounds to the chest wall.

stem: A chronic smoker has clubbing with an angle >180° at the nail bed. Which condition most strongly associates with this finding?
rationale: Digital clubbing reflects chronic tissue hypoxia—commonly seen with interstitial lung disease (fibrosis) and some malignancies.
